summary: Iteration 6 regression testing for Render build-config change (date-fns 4→^3.6.0 downgrade + corepack/yarn on Render). Ran backend regression suite (backend_test.py + test_iter4_guest_flow.py) — all 31/31 passed. Frontend smoke on preview URL: /, /products, /cart, /guest-checkout, /register all returned HTTP 200 with the app rendered. Signup on /register with a fresh email worked end-to-end: redirected to /, httpOnly access_token + refresh_token cookies set (SameSite=None, Secure), and /api/auth/me returned 200 with the new customer profile. Only console errors observed were guest-side 401s from /api/auth/me polling — same as iter5, not new. Per E1 instruction, the 7 stale tests in test_iter3_reviews_razorpay_cors.py were not re-run and are not flagged.
critical_code_review_comments: date-fns is not imported anywhere under /app/frontend/src (grep confirms). The downgrade is purely to satisfy react-day-picker@8.10.1's peer range (date-fns 2.x||3.x). react-day-picker itself is only used inside components/ui/calendar.jsx (unused shadcn scaffold). Consider removing both dependencies entirely in a follow-up cleanup PR to eliminate the peer-conflict surface area on future npm-based builds.

render.yaml frontend build now depends on corepack activating yarn@1.22.22. This is fine but couples deploy to Node 20+ (corepack shipped in Node 16.9+, but the auto-download requires internet at build time on Render). NODE_VERSION=20.11.1 in render.yaml covers this — good.
yarn.lock is now git-tracked (good); ensure package-lock.json is either absent or gitignored to avoid npm/yarn drift on future Render builds.
